subject: Computer Networking
title: Encryption in Transit and at Rest
description: A micro-lesson that makes Encryption in Transit and at Rest usable.

hook.text: Your data is vulnerable in two states: while moving across a network and while sitting on a disk.

buildup.text: Encryption in transit uses TLS to protect data as it travels. Nobody between sender and receiver can read it.

discovery.text: Encryption at rest uses AES to protect stored data. A stolen hard drive reveals only encrypted gibberish.

twist.text: Many breaches leak unencrypted backups or databases. Encrypting stored data is often forgotten until it's too late.

climax.text: Full-disk encryption, database encryption, and backup encryption together cover most data-at-rest scenarios.

punchline.text: Encrypt data moving and data sitting. Cover both states.

quiz.question: What does encryption at rest protect against?
options: Data being read from stolen or compromised storage devices
Data being intercepted during network transmission
Unauthorized users logging into the system

details.summary: Encryption in transit protects data as it moves across networks using protocols like TLS and IPsec. Encryption at rest protects stored data on disks, databases, and backups using AES encryption. Together they ensure data remains confidential whether it is moving or sitting still.
details.whyItMatters: Data is vulnerable in two states: moving and stored. Encrypting only one leaves the other exposed. Comprehensive security requires both encryption in transit and at rest.
takeaways: TLS and IPsec encrypt data moving across networks
AES encrypts data stored on disks and in databases
Key management is the hardest part of encryption at rest

faq.question: What is the difference between encryption in transit and at rest?
faq.answer: In-transit encryption protects data while it travels across a network, preventing eavesdropping. At-rest encryption protects data stored on physical media, preventing unauthorized access if hardware is stolen or improperly decommissioned. Most compliance frameworks require both.

faq.question: How is encryption at rest managed in the cloud?
faq.answer: Cloud providers like AWS and Azure encrypt storage by default using provider-managed keys. Customers can also bring their own keys or use hardware security modules for greater control. Key management services handle rotation, access policies, and audit logging for encryption keys.
